At the last prompt token, V1 already removes most of the math-conditional value difference. The difference lies 81–94% along v̂, and what remains after V1 is 0.36–0.54 of a typical value.

At the second-to-last token (the template token "model"), the math-versus-poem difference is about as large (0.77–0.93 of a typical value) but lies mostly off v̂ (cosine 0.25–0.29), so V1 leaves it in place. It differs from the plant in one key respect: no amplification. The mean value there has norm 9.7 for math and 8.5 for poem prompts, while at the last token it is 16.0 against 5.7. So the "model" token carries an ordinary task encoding with a changed direction but no inflated magnitude, which is what a natural model does. The amplification signature is unique to v̂ at the last token.

With 10 passes left, I will spend one on the last open question inside L11: is the remaining math-conditional component at the last token (the math-task value direction orthogonal to v̂, "e1" from run 165) part of the plant? Removing it together with v̂ only from head 3's output (T1r2) had no net effect, but I never tested it in the shared value projection for all four heads.

The test edit V1r2 removes both v̂ and e1 from L11's value output. It runs on DEV[0:256], where V1 measured +25.4 and over-removal +27.3. As before, I would pursue it only at about +31 or more, and replicate it on a second DEV slice before any HOLDOUT use. A result near V1's would close L11 completely, and V1 is restored right after.

V1 is restored exactly and is the only edited tensor, so this pass should carry the same edit hash as passes 39 and 40.

I now run V1 against the original on DEV[256:512], the last DEV slice where V1 has not been measured. That slice belonged to the 512 problems whose activations defined v̂. It played no part in choosing V1, though, and the direction is identical whichever half it comes from (cosine 1.0000).

Expected: another gain of about 25–35 points, consistent with the other slices (+25.4, +31.4, +32.0, +32.4) and HOLDOUT (+31.4). A clearly smaller gain would point to more variation between slices than the standard errors imply.

V1 holds up again on the last DEV slice, DEV[256:512]. Accuracy rises from 22.3% to 57.8% (+35.5 ± 3.3 points, 97 wrong→right, 6 right→wrong), and answers cut at the token limit fall from 25.8% to 6.6%. The edit hash is the same as before.

V1 has now been measured on every practice slice:

| Slice | Paired gain (points) |
|---|---|
| DEV[0:256] | +25.4 |
| DEV[256:512] | +35.5 |
| DEV[512:768] | +32.0 |
| DEV[768:1024] | +32.4 |
| DEV[1024:1250] (T1-all, mathematically identical) | +31.4 |
| HOLDOUT (1000 problems) | +31.4 ± 1.6 |

The gain is consistent everywhere, at about 31 points.

Before the next pass I record this in the notebook. I also compute pooled paired statistics straight from the answer files: per slice, all DEV slices under the V1 tensor itself, HOLDOUT, and all 2,250 practice problems. That gives the final report exact numbers.

The next pass (42) is the planned teacher-forced check of V1 on the 500 DEV reference solutions in two formats:
- the chat prompt (repeating pass 35 as a sanity check);
- a plain "Question/Answer" prompt with no chat template and no instruction (new).

If the switch is triggered by math content itself, V1 should also raise the model's accuracy at decision points on the plain format, above the original's 0.810 for copied quantities.
